evals.expected_output: Skill identifies GitLab as the host and loads its adapter, fetches MR metadata, searches for a ticket reference in the title/description, fetches diffs, attempts to locate the local clone and create an isolated review worktree pinned to the MR's head SHA, reviews across all five Code Review Pyramid layers (invoking the code-review-pyramid skill if available), posts concise inline comments via scripts/post_review_notes_gitlab.py (each ending with a 🤖, plus one positionless note reading 'Code reviewed using <model> 🤖'), removes the worktree, and outputs the review summary in the conversation (does NOT post it to the MR), including a 'Worth your own look' section naming Layer 1-2 files. Does NOT approve or submit the review.
expectations: Skill identifies the host from the URL shape and reads references/hosts/gitlab.md before fetching anything
Inline comments are posted via scripts/post_review_notes_gitlab.py rather than hand-written glab api calls

Each inline comment ends with a trailing 🤖 and a single positionless comment attributes the review (e.g. 'Code reviewed using Sonnet 5 (high) 🤖'), with an effort parenthetical only when one is genuinely known — never a guessed value

Inline comments default to 2-4 sentences of continuous prose (longer only for findings whose mechanism genuinely needs it, e.g. concurrency or security) and do not contain a separately labeled 'Failure scenario:' sub-paragraph
The review summary is output in the conversation, not posted to the MR
The conversation summary starts with '## Code Review Summary' and includes a Coverage line naming only the layers with posted comments (or 'no comments posted')

The conversation summary includes a 'Worth your own look' section listing a short, selectively-chosen set of files (Layer 1 API Semantics and/or Layer 2 Implementation Semantics — new/changed public contracts or business-rule-bearing logic), with files sharing the same reason grouped into one line, and no note about what's lower priority
The review covers Implementation Semantics and API Semantics (bottom layers)
The skill attempts to invoke the code-review-pyramid skill, or falls back to its own judgment if unavailable
The skill attempts to locate a local clone and create an isolated review worktree (never checking out the branch in the user's main clone), or notes the limitation if not found
The skill does not call any approve, submit, or review-completion API endpoint
If a ticket is found in the MR, the summary references it

evals.prompt: Can you do a code review on https://gitlab.com/acme/platform/-/merge_requests/7? There's no ticket for this one, it's a quick hotfix.
evals.expected_output: Skill reviews the MR without ticket context. The conversation summary explicitly states no ticket was found. Review still covers all pyramid layers. Inline comments are posted where issues exist. Skill attempts to create an isolated review worktree locally rather than checking out the branch in place.
expectations: Conversation summary states no ticket was found
Inline comments are still posted (review proceeds without ticket context)

Each inline comment ends with a trailing 🤖 and a single positionless comment attributes the review (e.g. 'Code reviewed using Sonnet 5 (high) 🤖'), with an effort parenthetical only when one is genuinely known — never a guessed value
The review summary is output in the conversation, not posted to the MR
The skill does not halt or ask for a ticket — it continues without one
The skill attempts to locate a local clone and create an isolated review worktree, or notes the limitation if not found

evals.prompt: Please review https://gitlab.com/acme/backend/-/merge_requests/201 — the ticket is GH-4521 in the MR title
evals.expected_output: Skill finds GH-4521 in the MR title, identifies it as a JIRA-style key, loads references/trackers/jira.md, fetches the ticket details, and uses the acceptance criteria to evaluate whether the implementation satisfies the requirements. expectations: Ticket GH-4521 is fetched via the JIRA tracker adapter and referenced in the summary
At least one inline comment references the ticket's requirements
The review summary is output in the conversation and links to the ticket
The review summary is not posted to the MR

Each inline comment ends with a footer starting 'Co-reviewed with :robot:' and naming the reviewing model (e.g. 'using Sonnet 5'), with an effort parenthetical only when one is genuinely known — never a guessed value

evals.expected_output: Skill identifies GitHub as the host and loads references/hosts/github.md, fetches PR metadata via gh pr view, searches for a ticket reference, fetches diffs via gh api .../pulls/123/files, creates an isolated review worktree at ~/projects/acme/my-service, reviews across all five pyramid layers, posts inline comments as a single GitHub pending review via scripts/post_review_notes_github.py (each comment ending with a 🤖, and the review body reading 'Code reviewed using <model> 🤖'), removes the worktree, and outputs the summary in the conversation with submit instructions referencing GitHub's Files changed / Review changes UI. Does not submit the review itself.
expectations: Skill identifies GitHub as the host from the URL shape and reads references/hosts/github.md before fetching anything
Inline comments are posted via scripts/post_review_notes_github.py as a single pending review, not via hand-written gh api calls
Each inline comment ends with a trailing 🤖 and the pending review's body attributes the review, naming the reviewing model (e.g. 'Code reviewed using Sonnet 5 🤖')
The review summary is output in the conversation, not posted to the PR
The summary's submit instructions reference GitHub's own UI (Files changed / Review changes), not GitLab's
The skill attempts to locate a local clone and create an isolated review worktree at the GitHub owner/repo path, or notes the limitation if not found

evals.prompt: Review https://github.com/acme/webapp/pull/88 — it's linked to issue acme/webapp#45
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies the ticket reference as a GitHub issue (not JIRA), loads references/trackers/github.md, fetches the issue via gh issue view, and uses its body as the requirements ground truth. The conversation summary links to the GitHub issue rather than a JIRA ticket.
expectations: Skill correctly identifies the GitHub issue reference and loads the GitHub tracker adapter rather than the JIRA one
The GitHub issue is fetched and referenced in the summary
At least one inline comment or the summary references the issue's stated requirements
The review summary is output in the conversation and is not posted to the PR or the issue
